label: lem:combination
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Smolyak combination identity

title: Proof
body_md:
Since only the operators $P_0,\ldots,P_n$ occur in \eqref{eq:abstractcombination}, we may assume that $P_k=0$ for $k>n$. For $1\le i\le d$, define the operator-valued polynomials
\[
 \mathcal P^{(i)}(z):=\sum_{m\ge0}P_m^{(i)}z^m,
 \qquad
 \mathcal D^{(i)}(z):=\sum_{m\ge0}D_m^{(i)}z^m.
\]
By the definition of $D_m$,
\[
 \mathcal D^{(i)}(z)=(1-z)\mathcal P^{(i)}(z).
\]
Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{3-2}
 \frac1{1-z}\prod_{i=1}^d\mathcal D^{(i)}(z)
 =(1-z)^{d-1}\prod_{i=1}^d\mathcal P^{(i)}(z).
\end{equation}
The coefficient of $z^n$ on the left-hand side of \eqref{3-2} is
\begin{equation}\label{3-3}
 \sum_{|\nu|_1\le n}D_{\nu_1}^{(1)}\cdots D_{\nu_d}^{(d)}.
\end{equation}
On the other hand, since
\[
 (1-z)^{d-1}=\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}(-1)^j\binom{d-1}{j}z^j,
\]
the coefficient of $z^n$ on the right-hand side is
\begin{equation}\label{3-4}
 \sum_{j=0}^{d-1}(-1)^j\binom{d-1}{j}
 \sum_{|\nu|_1=n-j}P_{\nu_1}^{(1)}\cdots P_{\nu_d}^{(d)},
\end{equation}
where an inner sum is understood to be zero when $n-j<0$. Comparing \eqref{3-3} and \eqref{3-4} proves the lemma.
head: environment

label: decom
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and set
\[
 r:=\left\lceil\frac{d-1}{\varepsilon}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 q:=N^{1/r},
 \qquad
 M_j:=\lceil q^j\rceil,
 \quad 0\le j\le r.
\]
Then $M_0=1$ and $M_r=N$. Define
\[
 T_j:=V_{M_j},\quad 0\le j\le r,
 \qquad
 T_j:=T_r=V_N,\quad j>r,
\]
and put
\[
 \Delta_0:=T_0,
 \qquad
 \Delta_j:=T_j-T_{j-1},\quad j\ge1.
\]
Since $T_r$ reproduces every trigonometric polynomial of degree at most $N$, we have
\begin{equation}\label{decom}
 g=T_rg=\sum_{j=0}^r\Delta_jg
   =\sum_{j=0}^\infty\Delta_jg,
 \qquad g\in\mathcal T([-N,N]).
\end{equation}
Moreover, $\Delta_j=0$ for $j>r$, and the reproduction property of $V_n$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{3-5:eq}
 \Delta_j e^{\mathrm i kt}=0
 \qquad\text{whenever }j\ge 1\text{ and }|k|\le q^{j-1}.
\end{equation}

For $\nu=(\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_d)\in\mathbb Z_+^d$, define
\[
 T_\nu:=T_{\nu_1}^{(1)}\cdots T_{\nu_d}^{(d)},
 \qquad
 \Delta_\nu:=\Delta_{\nu_1}^{(1)}\cdots\Delta_{\nu_d}^{(d)}.
\]
Applying \eqref{decom} in each variable yields
\begin{equation}\label{3-7-0}
 f=\sum_{\nu_1=0}^r\cdots\sum_{\nu_d=0}^r\Delta_\nu f
  =\sum_{\nu\in\mathbb Z_+^d}\Delta_\nu f,
 \qquad f\in\mathcal T(N,d).
\end{equation}

Let
\[
 L:=r+d-1.
\]
We claim that
\begin{equation}\label{3-7}
 \Delta_\nu f=0\   \ \text{whenever}
 \qquad f\in\mathcal T(N,d)\  \ \text{and}\  \  |\nu|_1>L.
\end{equation}
 Assume that $\Delta_\nu f\neq 0$ for some
$f\in\mathcal T(N,d)$. Then there must exist a vector   $\boldsymbol{k}=(k_1,\ldots,k_d)\in\Gamma(N,d)$
such that
\[
 \Delta_\nu e^{\mathrm i\langle\boldsymbol{k},\boldsymbol{x}\rangle}=\prod_{j=1}^d  \Delta_{\nu_j}[ e^{\mathrm i k_j x_j }] \neq 0.
\]
By \eqref{3-5:eq}, this implies that
$|k_j|> q^{v_j-1}$  whenever  $\nu_j\ge 1$, whereas if $\nu_j=0$, then   
$$\max\{|k_j|, 1\}\ge 1 > q^{-1}=q^{v_j-1}.$$  Consequently, in either case, 
\[ \max\{|k_j|,1\}> q^{v_j-1},\   \  j=1,\ldots, d.\]
Multiplying these inequalities over $j=1,\ldots, d$ and using $\boldsymbol{k}\in\Gamma(N,d)$, we obtain
\[
 q^{v_1+\cdots+v_d-d}
 <\prod_{i=1}^d\max\{|k_i|,1\}
 \le N=q^r.
\]
This implies
\[
 v_1+\cdots+v_d\le r+d-1=L,
\]
and hence  prove  the claim \eqref{3-7}.

Combining \eqref{3-7-0} and \eqref{3-7}, we obtain
\[
 f=\sum_{|\nu|_1\le L}\Delta_\nu f.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:combination}, applied with $P_j=T_j$ and $D_j=\Delta_j$, now gives the exact representation
\begin{equation}\label{eq:generalcombination}
 f=\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}(-1)^j\binom{d-1}{j}
 \sum_{|\nu|_1=L-j}T_\nu f.
\end{equation}

For $0\le i\le r$, set $\Lambda_i:=G_{M_i}$, and set $\Lambda_i:=G_N$ for $i>r$. Given $\nu\in\mathbb Z_+^d$, define the tensor-product grid
\[
 W_\nu:=\Lambda_{\nu_1}\times\cdots\times\Lambda_{\nu_d}.
\]
Iterating \eqref{eq:Vn-stability} in the $d$ variables gives
\begin{equation}\label{3-13}
 \lVert T_\nu\varphi\rVert_\infty
 \le A^d\lVert \varphi\rVert_{W_\nu},
 \qquad \varphi\in C(\mathbb T^d).
\end{equation}
Indeed, one first applies \eqref{eq:Vn-stability} in the first variable, then in the second variable, and so on; after $d$ steps, the right-hand side is the maximum of $|\varphi|$ over $W_\nu$.

Define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:generalW}
 W_{d,r}(N):=
 \bigcup_{j=0}^{d-1}\
 \bigcup_{|\nu|_1=L-j}W_\nu.
\end{equation}
Using \eqref{eq:generalcombination}, \eqref{3-13}, and the identity
\[
 \bigl|\{\nu\in\mathbb Z_+^d:|\nu|_1=s\}\bigr|
 =\binom{s+d-1}{d-1},
\]
we obtain
\begin{align*}
 \lVert f\rVert_\infty
 &\le A^d\lVert f\rVert_{W_{d,r}(N)}
 \sum_{j=0}^{d-1}\binom{d-1}{j}
 \binom{L-j+d-1}{d-1}\\
 &\le 2^{d-1}A^d\binom{r+2d-2}{d-1}
 \lVert f\rVert_{W_{d,r}(N)}.
\end{align*}
The standard estimate
\[
 \binom ab\le\left(\frac{ea}{b}\right)^b,
 \qquad a>b\ge1,
\]
together with $r\le(d-1)\varepsilon^{-1}+1$, gives
\begin{align*}
 2^{d-1}A^d\binom{r+2d-2}{d-1}
 &\le 2^{d-1}A^d
 \left(\frac{e(r+2d-2)}{d-1}\right)^{d-1}\\
 &\le \bigl(6eA^2(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\bigr)^{d-1}.
\end{align*}
Therefore,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:generalnorm-proof}
 \lVert f\rVert_\infty
 \le \bigl(6eA^2(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\bigr)^{d-1}
 \lVert f\rVert_{W_{d,r}(N)},
 \qquad f\in\mathcal T(N,d).
\end{equation}

It remains to estimate the cardinality of $W_{d,r}(N)$. Since $M_j\le2q^j$ for $0\le j\le r$, for every $\nu\in\mathbb Z_+^d$ we have
\[
 |W_\nu|
 =\prod_{i=1}^d|G_{M_{\min\{\nu_i,r\}}}|
 \le 8^d q^{|\nu|_1}.
\]
For the multi-indices occurring in \eqref{eq:generalW}, one has $r\le|\nu|_1\le r+d-1$. Hence
\begin{align*}
 |W_{d,r}(N)|
 &\le\sum_{s=r}^{r+d-1}\sum_{|\nu|_1=s}|W_\nu|\\
 &\le 8^d q^{r+d-1}
 \sum_{s=r}^{r+d-1}\binom{s+d-1}{d-1}\\
 &\le 8^d d\,N^{1+(d-1)/r}
 \binom{r+2d-2}{d-1}\\
 &\le \bigl(96(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\bigr)^{d-1}N^{1+\varepsilon}.
\end{align*}
Finally, set
\[
 W_{d,\varepsilon}(N):=W_{d,r}(N).
\]
Then \eqref{eq:generalnorm-proof} and the last cardinality estimate prove \eqref{eq:generalnorm-1-5} and \eqref{eq:generalcard-1-4}, respectively, with $C_1=96$ and $C_2=6eA^2$.
head: environment

label: thm:HC-obstruction
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $\boldsymbol{x}=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)\in[-\pi,\pi)^d$, define
\[
 F(\boldsymbol{x}):=\prod_{j=1}^d\cos^2\left(\frac{x_j}{2}\right)
 =\frac1{4^d}\prod_{j=1}^d\bigl(e^{\mathrm i x_j}+e^{-\mathrm i x_j}+2\bigr).
\]
Then $F\in\mathcal T(1,d)$, $0\le F\le1$, and $\lVert F\rVert_\infty=F(0)=1$. Since $\mathcal T(1,d)$ is translation invariant, $F(\cdot-\boldsymbol{a})\in\mathcal T(1,d)$ for every $\boldsymbol{a}\in\mathbb T^d$. It follows from \eqref{4-1} that, for every $\boldsymbol{a}\in\mathbb T^d$, there exists $\boldsymbol{w}\in W$ such that
\[
 F(\boldsymbol{w}-\boldsymbol{a})\ge B^{-1}.
\]
Set
\[
 E_B:=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in[-\pi,\pi)^d:F(\boldsymbol{x})\ge B^{-1}\}.
\]
The preceding observation gives the covering
\[
 [-\pi,\pi)^d=\bigcup_{\boldsymbol{w}\in W}(\boldsymbol{w}-E_B),
\]
and hence
\begin{equation}\label{4-3}
 |W|\mu_d(E_B)\ge1.
\end{equation}

It remains to estimate the measure of $E_B$. Since for $|t|\le\pi$,
\[
 \cos (t/2)\le e^{-t^2/8},
\]
it follows that
\[
 F(\boldsymbol{x})\le\exp\left(-\frac{|\boldsymbol{x}|^2}{4}\right),
 \qquad \boldsymbol{x}\in[-\pi,\pi)^d.
\]
Hence,
\[
 E_B\subset\{\boldsymbol{x}\in[-\pi,\pi)^d:|\boldsymbol{x}|^2\le4\log B\}.
\]
If $\omega_d$ denotes the volume of the Euclidean unit ball in $\mathbb R^d$, then
\[
 \mu_d(E_B)
 \le\frac{\omega_d(2\sqrt{\log B})^d}{(2\pi)^d}
 =\omega_d\left(\frac{\sqrt{\log B}}{\pi}\right)^d.
\]
Using
\[
 \omega_d=\frac{\pi^{d/2}}{\Gamma(d/2+1)}
 \le\left(\frac{2\pi e}{d}\right)^{d/2},
\]
we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:EB-measure}
 \mu_d(E_B)\le
 \left(\frac{2e\log B}{\pi d}\right)^{d/2}.
\end{equation}
Combining \eqref{4-3} and \eqref{eq:EB-measure} proves \eqref{eq:HC-lower}.
head: environment

label: thm:transfer
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:transfer}
Let $V$ be a translation-invariant linear subspace of $C(\mathbb T^d)$ with
\[
 \dim_{\mathbb R}V=n_0<\infty.
\]
Assume that there exist a constant $B\ge2$ and a finite set $W\subset\mathbb T^d$, with $|W|=m_0$, such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:transfer-deterministic}
 \lVert f\rVert_\infty\le B\lVert f\rVert_W,
 \qquad f\in V.
\end{equation}
Then, for every $\eta\in(0,1)$ and every integer
\begin{equation}\label{eq:transfer-m}
 m\ge m_0\left(n_0\log(5B)+\log\frac1\eta\right),
\end{equation}
one has, with probability at least $1-\eta$,
\[
 \lVert f\rVert_\infty\le4B\lVert f\rVert_{X_m},
 \qquad f\in V.
\]
head: environment

label: cor:N2
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:N2}
Let $d,N\ge2$, $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, and $\eta\in(0,1)$. There exist constants $B_{\varepsilon,d}>0$ and $C(d,\varepsilon)>0$ such that
\[
 m_*\bigl(N,d,B_{\varepsilon,d},\eta\bigr)
 \le C(d,\varepsilon)N^{2+\varepsilon}
 \left(1+\log\frac1\eta\right).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm-1-1} with $\varepsilon/2$ in place of $\varepsilon$. The resulting deterministic norming set has cardinality
\[
 m_0\le C(d,\varepsilon)N^{1+\varepsilon/2},
\]
and its norming constant depends only on $d$ and $\varepsilon$. Moreover,
\[
 n_0:=\dim_{\mathbb R}\mathcal T(N,d)
 \le C_dN\log^{d-1}(2N).
\]
Theorem~\ref{thm:transfer} therefore applies once
\[
 m\ge C(d,\varepsilon)N^{1+\varepsilon/2}
 \left(N\log^{d-1}(2N)+\log\frac1\eta\right).
\]
Since $\log^{d-1}(2N)\le C(d,\varepsilon)N^{\varepsilon/2}$ for $N\ge2$, the asserted estimate follows.
head: environment

label: thm:remez
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $f\in V$. For every $\boldsymbol{a}\in\mathbb T^d$, translation invariance and \eqref{5-3a} give
\[
 \lVert f\rVert_\infty
 =\lVert f(\cdot-\boldsymbol{a})\rVert_\infty
 \le B\lVert f(\cdot-\boldsymbol{a})\rVert_W.
\]
Thus, for every $\boldsymbol{a}\in\mathbb T^d$, there exists $\boldsymbol{w}\in W$ such that
\[
 |f(\boldsymbol{w}-\boldsymbol{a})|\ge B^{-1}\lVert f\rVert_\infty.
\]
Equivalently, $\boldsymbol{a}\in\boldsymbol{w}-S_f(B)$, and therefore
\[
 \mathbb T^d=\bigcup_{\boldsymbol{w}\in W}\bigl(\boldsymbol{w}-S_f(B)\bigr).
\]
Taking Haar measure proves \eqref{5-2}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Lemma~\ref{thm:remez} immediately yields a Nikolskii inequality. Indeed, for $0<p<\infty$ and $f\in V$,
\[
 \lVert f\rVert_p^p
 \ge\int_{S_f(B)}|f(\boldsymbol{x})|^p\,d\mu_d(\boldsymbol{x})
 \ge\frac1{|W|}\left(\frac{\lVert f\rVert_\infty}{B}\right)^p.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \lVert f\rVert_\infty\le B|W|^{1/p}\lVert f\rVert_p,
 \qquad f\in V.
\]
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Applying Lemma~\ref{thm:remez} to the norming set supplied by Theorem~\ref{thm-1-1}, we obtain, for every $f\in\mathcal T(N,d)$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$,
\[
 \mu_d\bigl(S_f(B_\varepsilon)\bigr)
 \ge\frac1{A_\varepsilon N^{1+\varepsilon}},
\]
where
\begin{equation}\label{5-3}
 B_\varepsilon:=\bigl(C_2(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\bigr)^d,
 \qquad
 A_\varepsilon:=\bigl(C_1(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\bigr)^d.
\end{equation}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let
\[
 \delta:=\frac1{2B}
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 \mathcal B:=\{f\in V:\lVert f\rVert_\infty\le1\}.
\]
Choose a maximal $\delta$-separated subset $\mathcal N$ of $\mathcal B$ in the uniform norm. Since $V$ has real dimension $n_0$, the standard volumetric estimate gives
\[
 |\mathcal N|
 \le\left(1+\frac2\delta\right)^{n_0}
 =(1+4B)^{n_0}
 \le(5B)^{n_0}.
\]
By maximality, $\mathcal N$ is also a $\delta$-net of $\mathcal B$. Furthermore, by Lemma~\ref{thm:remez},
\[
 \mu_d(S_g(B))\ge\frac1{m_0},
 \qquad g\in\mathcal N.
\]

For a nonzero $g\in V$,
\begin{equation}\label{5-6}
 X_m\cap S_g(B)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \lVert g\rVert_\infty\le B\lVert g\rVert_{X_m}.
\end{equation}
Let $E$ be the event that $X_m\cap S_g(B)\ne\varnothing$ for every $g\in\mathcal N$.
Then
\[ E^c= \bigcup_{g\in\mathcal N} \Bigl\{ X_m\cap S_g(B)=\varnothing \Bigr\}=\bigcup_{g\in\mathcal N} \Bigl\{ \xi^j\notin S_g(B),\  \ \forall 1\leq j\leq m\Bigr\}.\]
Therefore, independence, the union bound, and \eqref{eq:transfer-m}  imply
\begin{align*}
 \mathbf{P}(E^c)
 &\le |\mathcal N|\sup_{g\in\mathcal N}
 \bigl(1-\mu_d(S_g(B))\bigr)^m\le(5B)^{n_0}\left(1-\frac1{m_0}\right)^m\\
 &\le\exp\left(n_0\log(5B)-\frac{m}{m_0}\right)
 \le\eta.
\end{align*}

Assume that $E$ occurs, and let $f\in V$ with $\lVert f\rVert_\infty=1$. Choose $g\in\mathcal N$ such that $\lVert f-g\rVert_\infty\le\delta$. Then $\lVert g\rVert_\infty\ge1-\delta$, while \eqref{5-6} gives $\lVert g\rVert_\infty\le B\lVert g\rVert_{X_m}$. Hence
\begin{align*}
 \lVert f\rVert_{X_m}
 &\ge\lVert g\rVert_{X_m}-\lVert f-g\rVert_\infty\\
 &\ge\frac{1-\delta}{B}-\delta
 =\frac{B-1}{2B^2}
 \ge\frac1{4B}.
\end{align*}
By homogeneity,
\[
 \lVert f\rVert_\infty\le4B\lVert f\rVert_{X_m},
 \qquad f\in V.
\]
Since $\mathbf{P}(E)\ge1-\eta$, the proof is complete.
head: environment

label: thm:abstract
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:abstract}
Let $\theta\in(0,1]$, set $\ell:=\lceil3/\theta\rceil$, and let $\eta\in(0,1)$. If
\begin{equation}\label{eq:samplesize}
 m\ge3C_K^2K^2r^{1+\theta}
 \log\left(\frac{2Kr}{\eta}\right),
\end{equation}
then, with probability at least $1-\eta$,
\[
 \lVert F\rVert_\infty
 \le B(K,\theta)\lVert F\rVert_{\Omega_m},
 \qquad F\in V,
\]
where
\[
 B(K,\theta):=2\ell M_K^\ell.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 B(K,\theta)\le\exp\left(\frac{CK}{\theta}\right)
\]
for an absolute constant $C>0$.
head: environment

label: lem:annih
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:annih}
Define
\[
 h_K(z):=\prod_{j=1}^K\left(1-\frac Kj z\right)
 =\sum_{j=0}^Kb_jz^j.
\]
Then the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]
 \item There is a polynomial $Q_K(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}c_jz^j$ such that
 \[
  1-h_K(z)=zQ_K(z),
  \qquad c_j=-b_{j+1},\quad 0\le j\le K-1.
 \]
 \item One has
 \[
  \sum_{j=0}^K|b_j|=M_K=\binom{2K}{K}\le4^K,
  \qquad
  \sum_{j=0}^{K-1}|c_j|\le M_K.
 \]
 \item $h_K(S)F=0$ for every $F\in V$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $h_K(0)=1$, the polynomial $1-h_K$ is divisible by $z$, and comparison of coefficients gives $c_j=-b_{j+1}$. This proves (i).

The coefficients of $h_K$ alternate in sign. Therefore,
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{j=0}^K|b_j|
 &=h_K(-1)
 =\prod_{s=1}^K\left(1+\frac Ks\right)\\
 &=\frac{(K+1)(K+2)\cdots(2K)}{K!}
 =\binom{2K}{K}
 \le4^K.
\end{align*}
It follows also that
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^{K-1}|c_j|
 =\sum_{j=1}^K|b_j|
 =M_K-1\le M_K.
\]
This proves (ii).

To prove (iii), apply \eqref{6-5} with $U=h_K$. If $\omega\ne0$, then $|\omega|_1\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$, and hence
\[
 h_K\left(\frac{|\omega|_1}{K}\right)=0.
\]
Thus $h_K(S)F=0$ for every $F\in V$.
head: environment

label: lem:leverage
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: 6-11a
title: Proof
body_md:
We first claim that
\begin{equation}\label{6-11a}
 \langle P_VF,F\rangle
 \le\sum_{j=1}^K\langle P_jF,F\rangle,
 \qquad F\in L^2(\Omega,\mu).
\end{equation}
Indeed, by \eqref{6-4} and \eqref{6-9},
\begin{align*}
 \langle P_VF,F\rangle
 &=\sum_{\omega\ne0}\lVert \Pi_\omega F\rVert_2^2\\
 &\le\sum_{j=1}^K\sum_{\omega:\,\omega_j=1}
 \lVert \Pi_\omega F\rVert_2^2
 =\sum_{j=1}^K\langle P_jF,F\rangle.
\end{align*}

The reproducing kernel of $H_j$ is
\[
 K_{H_j}(x,y)
 =r_j\sum_{A\in\mathcal P_j}\mathbf1_A(x)\mathbf1_A(y),
\]
and therefore
\begin{equation}\label{6-12-a}
 K_{H_j}(x,x)=r_j,
 \qquad x\in\Omega.
\end{equation}
For $u\in\Omega$, define $e_u:=|\Omega|\mathbf1_{\{u\}}$. Then
\[
 \langle F,e_u\rangle=F(u),
 \qquad F\in L^2(\Omega,\mu),
\]
and
\[
 K_V(u,u)=\langle P_Ve_u,e_u\rangle.
\]
Using \eqref{6-11a} and \eqref{6-12-a}, we obtain
\[
 K_V(u,u)
 \le\sum_{j=1}^K\langle P_je_u,e_u\rangle
 =\sum_{j=1}^Kr_j
 \le Kr.
\]
This proves the first assertion in \eqref{6-10a}.

Let $\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_n$ be an orthonormal basis of $V$, where $n=\dim V$. Since
\[
 K_V(x,y)=\sum_{s=1}^n\varphi_s(x)\overline{\varphi_s(y)},
\]
we have
\[
 n=\int_\Omega K_V(x,x)\,d\mu(x)\le Kr.
\]
Finally, the reproducing property and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality give
\begin{align*}
 |F(x)|
 &\le\lVert F\rVert_2
 \left(\int_\Omega|K_V(x,y)|^2\,d\mu(y)\right)^{1/2}\\
 &=\lVert F\rVert_2\sqrt{K_V(x,x)}
 \le\sqrt{Kr}\,\lVert F\rVert_2.
\end{align*}
Taking the maximum over $x\in\Omega$ proves \eqref{8-4-Nik}.

label: lem:chernoff
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Matrix Chernoff estimate

label: lem:hit
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:hit}
If the frame event \eqref{eq:frame} occurs, then every cell of every partition $\mathcal P_j$ contains at least one of the sample points $u_1,\ldots,u_m$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $A\in\mathcal P_j$. Since $\mathbf1_A\in H_j\subset V$ and $\lVert \mathbf1_A\rVert_2^2=\mu(A)>0$, the lower estimate in \eqref{eq:frame} gives
\[
 \frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m\mathbf1_A(u_i)
 =\lVert \mathbf1_A\rVert_{L^2(\Omega_m)}^2
 \ge(1-\delta)\mu(A)>0.
\]
Thus $u_i\in A$ for at least one $i$.
head: environment

label: lem:emp
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:emp}
Assume that the frame event \eqref{eq:frame} occurs with $0<\delta\le1/2$. Then the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]
 \item The form $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_m$ is an inner product on $V$, and $\widehat P_j|_V$ is the orthogonal projection of $(V,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_m)$ onto $H_j$.
 \item For every $F\in V$,
 \[
  \lVert \widehat P_jF\rVert_\infty\le\lVert F\rVert_{\Omega_m},
  \qquad
  \lVert \widehat SF\rVert_\infty\le\lVert F\rVert_{\Omega_m}.
 \]
 Consequently,
 \[
  \lVert \widehat P_j\rVert_{\infty\to\infty}\le1,
  \qquad
  \lVert \widehat S\rVert_{\infty\to\infty}\le1.
 \]
 \item For every $F\in V$,
 \begin{equation}\label{6-17c}
  \lVert (\widehat P_j-P_j)F\rVert_2\le2\delta\lVert F\rVert_2.
 \end{equation}
 Consequently,
 \[
  \lVert \widehat S-S\rVert_{2\to2}\le2\delta,
  \qquad
  \lVert \widehat S\rVert_{2\to2}\le2.
 \]
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The lower estimate in \eqref{eq:frame} shows that $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_m$ is positive definite on $V$. Hence, $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_m$  is an inner product on $V$.  For each $A\in {\mathcal P}_j$, let $\phi_A=\sqrt{\frac m {N_A}}\1_A$. A straightforward calculation shows that $\{ \phi_A:\  A\in{\mathcal P}_j\}$
is an orthonormal basis of $(H_j, \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_m)$, and
\[ \widehat P_jF= \sum_{A\in{\mathcal P}_j} \langle F,\phi_A\rangle_m\phi_A\in H_j.\]
Hence, $\widehat P_j|_V$ is the orthogonal projection of $(V,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_m)$ onto $H_j$.
This proves (i).

If $x\in A\in\mathcal P_j$, then
\[
 |\widehat P_jF(x)|
 =\left|\frac1{N_A}\sum_{i:\,u_i\in A}F(u_i)\right|
 \le\lVert F\rVert_{\Omega_m}.
\]
Taking the maximum over $x$ proves the first estimate in (ii), and averaging over $j$ gives the estimate for $\widehat S$. Since $\lVert F\rVert_{\Omega_m}\le\lVert F\rVert_\infty$, the operator-norm estimates follow.

It remains to prove (iii). Put
\[
 G:=(\widehat P_j-P_j)F\in H_j.
\]
The lower frame estimate gives
\begin{equation}\label{6-18b}
 (1-\delta)\lVert G\rVert_2^2
 \le\lVert G\rVert_{L^2(\Omega_m)}^2.
\end{equation}
Write
\[ G=(\widehat P_j F-F) +(F-P_jF).\]
Since $F-\widehat P_jF$ is orthogonal to $H_j$ with respect to $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_m$, while $F-P_jF$ is orthogonal to $H_j$ in $L^2(\Omega,\mu)$, we have
\begin{align}
 \lVert G\rVert_{L^2(\Omega_m)}^2
 &=\langle F-P_jF,G\rangle_m\notag\\
 &=\langle F-P_jF,G\rangle_m
   -\langle F-P_jF,G\rangle.
 \label{6-18}
\end{align}
Using \eqref{6-16a} and the fact that $P_j$ is an orthogonal projection, we obtain
\[
 \lVert G\rVert_{L^2(\Omega_m)}^2
 \le\delta\lVert F-P_jF\rVert_2\lVert G\rVert_2
 \le\delta\lVert F\rVert_2\lVert G\rVert_2.
\]
Together with \eqref{6-18b}, this gives
\[
 \lVert G\rVert_2=\lVert (\widehat P_j-P_j)F\rVert
 \le\frac{\delta}{1-\delta}\lVert F\rVert_2
 \le2\delta\lVert F\rVert_2,
\]
which proves \eqref{6-17c}. Averaging over $j$ yields
\[
 \lVert \widehat S-S\rVert_{2\to2}\le2\delta.
\]
Finally, since $\lVert S\rVert_{2\to2}\le1$, we have
\[
 \lVert \widehat S\rVert_{2\to2}
 \le\lVert S\rVert_{2\to2}+\lVert \widehat S-S\rVert_{2\to2}
 \le1+2\delta\le2.
\]
head: environment

label: lem:poly
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:poly}
Assume that the frame event \eqref{eq:frame} occurs with $0<\delta\le1/2$, and let
\[
 \Lambda:=h_K(\widehat S)
\]
as an operator on $V$. Then
\[
 \lVert \Lambda\rVert_{2\to2}\le C_K\delta,
 \qquad
 \lVert \Lambda\rVert_{\infty\to\infty}\le M_K,
 \qquad
 \lVert Q_K(\widehat S)\rVert_{\infty\to\infty}\le M_K.
\]
head: environment

label: 6-21a
title: Proof
body_md:
Set $A:=\widehat S$ and $B:=S$, regarded as operators on $V$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:emp},
\[
 \lVert A\rVert_{2\to2}\le2,
 \qquad
 \lVert B\rVert_{2\to2}\le1,
 \qquad
 \lVert A-B\rVert_{2\to2}\le2\delta.
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:annih}(iii), $h_K(B)=0$ on $V$. Therefore,
\begin{equation}\label{6-21a}
 \Lambda=h_K(A)-h_K(B)
 =\sum_{j=1}^Kb_j(A^j-B^j).
\end{equation}
For $1\le j\le K$, the identity
\[
 A^j-B^j
 =\sum_{i=0}^{j-1}A^{j-i-1}(A-B)B^i
\]
gives
\[
 \lVert A^j-B^j\rVert_{2\to2}
 \le2\delta\sum_{i=0}^{j-1}2^{j-i-1}
 \le2^{j+1}\delta.
\]
Substituting this estimate into \eqref{6-21a} and using Lemma~\ref{lem:annih}(ii), we obtain
\[
 \lVert \Lambda\rVert_{2\to2}
 \le\delta\sum_{j=1}^K2^{j+1}|b_j|
 \le2^{K+1}M_K\delta
 =C_K\delta.
\]

By Lemma~\ref{lem:emp}(ii), $\lVert A\rVert_{\infty\to\infty}\le1$. It follows that
\[
 \lVert \Lambda\rVert_{\infty\to\infty}
 \le\sum_{j=0}^K|b_j|\lVert A\rVert_{\infty\to\infty}^j
 \le M_K,
\]
and similarly,
\[
 \lVert Q_K(A)\rVert_{\infty\to\infty}
 \le\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}|c_j|\lVert A\rVert_{\infty\to\infty}^j
 \le M_K.
\]
head: environment

label: lem:amp
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $F\in V$. Lemmas~\ref{lem:leverage} and \ref{lem:poly} give
\[
 \lVert \Lambda^\ell F\rVert_\infty
 \le\sqrt{Kr}\,\lVert \Lambda^\ell F\rVert_2
 \le\sqrt{Kr}\,(C_K\delta)^\ell\lVert F\rVert_2.
\]
By the assumption on $\delta$,
\[
 C_K\delta\le K^{-1/2}r^{-\theta/2}.
\]
Since $\mu$ is a probability measure, it follows that
\begin{align*}
 \lVert \Lambda^\ell F\rVert_\infty
 &\le K^{(1-\ell)/2}r^{(1-\theta\ell)/2}\lVert F\rVert_\infty\le r^{(1-\theta\ell)/2}\lVert F\rVert_\infty.
\end{align*}
Here we used $\ell\ge3$ and $K\ge1$. Since $\theta\ell\ge3$ and $r\ge2$, we have
\[
 r^{(1-\theta\ell)/2}\le r^{-1}\le\frac12.
\]
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: An important aspect of the proofs above  is that they do not require the empirical projections $\widehat P_j$ to commute. Their uniform-norm contractivity is sufficient. Commutativity is used for the original projections, to obtain $h_K(S)=0$.
head: environment

label: lem:dlvp
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:dlvp}
The following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]
 \item For every $f\in\mathcal T([-N,N]^d)$,
 \[
  f=\sum_{\boldsymbol{n}\in[L]_0^d}\Psi_{\boldsymbol{n}}f.
 \]
 \item If $\boldsymbol{n}\in{\mathbb Z}_+^d$ and $f\in L^1(\mathbb T^d)$, then $\Psi_{\boldsymbol{n}}f$ is a trigonometric polynomial with spectrum contained in $J_{\boldsymbol{n}}$. In particular,
 \[
  \lVert \partial_j\Psi_{\boldsymbol{n}}f\rVert_\infty
  \le2^{n_j+1}\lVert \Psi_{\boldsymbol{n}}f\rVert_\infty,
  \qquad 1\le j\le d.
 \]
 \item There exists an absolute constant $A\ge1$ such that, for every $1\le p\le\infty$,
 \[
  \sup_{\boldsymbol{n}\in{\mathbb Z}_+^d}\lVert \Psi_{\boldsymbol{n}}f\rVert_p
  \le A^d\lVert f\rVert_p,
  \qquad f\in L^p(\mathbb T^d).
 \]
 In fact, one can choose here  $A=6$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: lem:cellwise
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:cellwise}
Let $\boldsymbol{n}\in{\mathbb Z}_+^d$, and suppose that $\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y}$ belong to the same box of ${\mathcal D}_{\boldsymbol{n}}$. Then, for every $f\in C(\mathbb T^d)$,
\[
 \lvert \Psi_{\boldsymbol{n}}f(\boldsymbol{x})-\Psi_{\boldsymbol{n}}f(\boldsymbol{y})\rvert
 \le\frac{2\pi dA^d}{\ell_0}\lVert f\rVert_\infty.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $f_{\boldsymbol{n}}:=\Psi_{\boldsymbol{n}}f$, and define
\[
 \boldsymbol{z}^0:=\boldsymbol{x},
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol{z}^j:=(y_1,\ldots,y_j,x_{j+1},\ldots,x_d),
 \quad 1\le j\le d.
\]
Since $\boldsymbol{x}$ and $\boldsymbol{y}$ belong to the same box of ${\mathcal D}_{\boldsymbol{n}}$,
\[
 |x_j-y_j|\le\frac{2\pi}{\ell_0 2^{n_j+1}},
 \qquad 1\le j\le d.
\]
Using Lemma~\ref{lem:dlvp}(ii) and (iii), we obtain
\begin{align*}
 |f_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{x})-f_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{y})|
 &\le\sum_{j=1}^d
 |f_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{z}^{j-1})-f_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{z}^j)|
 \le\sum_{j=1}^d\lVert \partial_jf_{\boldsymbol{n}}\rVert_\infty|x_j-y_j|\\
 &\le\sum_{j=1}^d2^{n_j+1}\lVert f_{\boldsymbol{n}}\rVert_\infty
 \frac{2\pi}{\ell_0 2^{n_j+1}}
 \le\frac{2\pi dA^d}{\ell_0}\lVert f\rVert_\infty.
\end{align*}
head: environment

label: lem:simplex
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:simplex}
If $\boldsymbol{n}\in{\mathbb Z}_+^d$ and $\Gamma(N,d)\cap J_{\boldsymbol{n}}\ne\emptyset$, then
\[
 |\boldsymbol{n}|_1<L+d.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose $\boldsymbol{k}=(k_1,\ldots,k_d)\in\Gamma(N,d)\cap J_{\boldsymbol{n}}$. If $n_j\ge1$, then
\[
 2^{n_j-1}<|k_j|<2^{n_j+1},
\]
whereas if $n_j=0$, then $|k_j|\le1$. Thus, in either case,
\[
 2^{n_j-1}<\max\{|k_j|,1\}.
\]
Multiplying these inequalities over $j=1,\ldots,d$ and using $\boldsymbol{k}\in\Gamma(N,d)$, we obtain
\[
 2^{|\boldsymbol{n}|_1-d}
 <\prod_{j=1}^d\max\{|k_j|,1\}
 \le N\le2^L.
\]
Hence $|\boldsymbol{n}|_1<L+d$.
head: environment

label: lem-7-4
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let   $\boldsymbol{n}=(n_1,\ldots, n_d)\in M_{L+d}$.
Then   $0\leq n_j\leq L$ for  $1\leq j\leq d$,  and hence
\begin{align*}
\Bigl\{ \boldsymbol{m}\in [L]_0^d:\  \ \boldsymbol{n}\prec \boldsymbol{m}\Bigr\}&=
\Bigl\{ \sum_{j=1}^d (n_j+k_j):\  \ k_j=0,1,\ldots, L-n_j,\  \ 1\leq j\leq d\Bigl\} \\
& =\Bigl\{ |\boldsymbol{n}|_1,  |\boldsymbol{n}|_1+1, \ldots, Ld\Bigr\}. \end{align*}
Since
$|\boldsymbol{n}|_1< L+d <Ld$,
 there must exist  $\boldsymbol{m}\in S_{L+d}$ such that $\boldsymbol{n}\prec \boldsymbol{m}$.
head: environment

label: lem:macro
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:macro}
The following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (a)]
 \item For every $\beta\in\mathcal{I}$, the partition $\mathcal{Q}_\beta$ is regular and $\mathcal{G}$-coarse.
 \item $|\mathcal{I}|\le dq^{d-1}$.
 \item The operators $P_\beta$, $\beta\in\mathcal{I}$, pairwise commute.
 \item For every ${\mathbf t}\in M_{L+d}\cup S_{L+d}$, there exists $\beta\in\mathcal{I}$ such that
 \[
  {\mathbf t}\preceq a(\beta).
 \]
 Consequently, $\mathcal{Q}_\beta$ refines ${\mathcal D}_{{\mathbf t}}$.
 \item For every $\beta\in\mathcal{I}$,
 \[
  |\mathcal{Q}_\beta|
  \le\ell_0^d2^{L+2d+d(h-1)}.
 \]
 Consequently,
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:macro-r}
  r:=\max_{\beta\in\mathcal{I}}|\mathcal{Q}_\beta|
  \le C_d\ell_0^dN^{1+d/q}.
 \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Part (a) follows from the definition of $\mathcal{Q}_\beta$ and the fact that $a(\beta)\preceq\boldsymbol{L}$. 

(b)  For each  $\beta\in \mathcal{I}$, there exists $\boldsymbol{n}\in C_\beta$ such that  $|\boldsymbol{n}|_1=L+d$. Since 
\[ n_j\in I_{\beta_j} \subset \Bigl\{ (\beta_j-1) h, (\beta_j-1) h+1, \ldots, \beta_j h-1\Bigr\},\]
we have
$$ (\beta_j-1) h \leq n_j<\beta_j h,\  \ 1\leq j\leq d.$$
Summing these inequalities  over $1\leq j\leq d$ gives 
\[ h (|\beta|_1-d) \leq |\boldsymbol{n}|_1 =L+d < |\beta|_1 h.\]
Therefore, 
\[ \frac {L+d} h <|\beta|_1 \leq \frac {L+d} h+d.\]
Define 
\[ A={\mathbb Z}\cap \Bigl( \frac {L+d} h, \frac {L+d} h +d\Bigr].\]
Then $|A|\leq d$ and the preceding estimate shows that $|\beta|_1\in A$ for every $\beta\in \mathcal{I}$. 
Thus, 
\[ \mathcal{I}\subset \Bigl\{ (\beta_1, \ldots, \beta_{d-1}, \ell-\sum_{j=1}^{d-1}\beta_j):\   \ \beta_j\in [q],\  1\leq j\leq d-1,\  \ \ell\in A\Bigr\}.\]
It follows that 
$$|\mathcal{I}|\leq |A| q^{d-1}\leq d q^{d-1}. $$





Part (c) follows from \eqref{7-3}.

(d)\  \ Let ${\mathbf t}\in M_{L+d}\cup S_{L+d}$. If ${\mathbf t}\in M_{L+d}$, by Lemma~\ref{lem-7-4}, we may choose  ${\mathbf s}\in S_{L+d}$ such that ${\mathbf t}\preceq{\mathbf s}$. If ${\mathbf t}\in S_{L+d}$, we put ${\mathbf s}:={\mathbf t}$. Since $\{C_\beta:\  \ \beta\in \{1,\ldots, q\}^d\}$ is a partition of $[L]_0^d$, there is a unique $\beta\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^d$ such that ${\mathbf s}\in C_\beta\cap S_{L+d}$. Then $\beta\in\mathcal{I}$, and the definition of $a(\beta)$ gives
\[
 {\mathbf t}\preceq{\mathbf s}\preceq a(\beta).
\]
Thus, $\mathcal{Q}_\beta={\mathcal D}_{a(\beta)}$ refines ${\mathcal D}_{{\mathbf t}}$.


(e)\  \ Fix $\beta\in\mathcal{I}$ and choose $\boldsymbol{n}\in C_\beta\cap S_{L+d}$. Then  $\boldsymbol{n}\preceq a(\beta)$ and
$n_j$ and $a(\beta)_j$ belong to the same interval $I_{\beta_j}$. Thus,
\[
 0\le a(\beta)_j-n_j\le  \operatorname{diam}(I_{\beta_j})=|I_{\beta_j}|-1\leq h-1,
 \qquad 1\le j\le d.
\]
It follows that
\[
 |a(\beta)|_1\le|\boldsymbol{n}|_1+d(h-1)=L+d+d(h-1).
\]
Using \eqref{7-2-b}, we obtain
\[
 |\mathcal{Q}_\beta|=|{\mathcal D}_{a(\beta)}|
 =(2\ell_0)^d2^{|a(\beta)|_1}
 \le\ell_0^d2^{L+2d+d(h-1)}.
\]
Since $2^L\le2N$ and $h-1<(L+1)/q$, the last estimate implies
\[
 |\mathcal{Q}_\beta|\le \ell_0^d 2^{2d+\frac dq}  2^{L(1+\frac dq)}\leq  C_d\ell_0^dN^{1+d/q}.
\]
Taking the maximum over $\beta\in\mathcal{I}$ proves \eqref{eq:macro-r}.
head: environment

label: prop:transfer
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Define
\[ \mathcal{A}(f):=\Bigl\{\boldsymbol{n}\in {\mathbb Z}_+^d:\   \ \Psi_{\boldsymbol{n}} f\   \ \text{is not identically zero}\Bigr\}.\]
 For each $\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathcal{A}(f)$, put $f_{\boldsymbol{n}}=\Psi_{\boldsymbol{n}} f$.
 By \eqref{eq:active-simplex},  $\mathcal{A}(f)\subset M_{L+d}$. Hence,
 by  Lemma~\ref{lem:macro}(d), for every $\boldsymbol{n}\in\mathcal{A}(f)$ there is a retained index $\beta(\boldsymbol{n})\in\mathcal{I}$ such that
\[
 \boldsymbol{n}\preceq a(\beta(\boldsymbol{n})),
\]
and hence $\mathcal{Q}_{\beta(\boldsymbol{n})}$ refines ${\mathcal D}_{\boldsymbol{n}}$.

For every $Q\in{\mathcal D}_{\boldsymbol{n}}$, choose a point $\boldsymbol{x}_{\boldsymbol{n},Q}\in Q$, and define
\[
 \widetilde g_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{x})
 :=\sum_{Q\in{\mathcal D}_{\boldsymbol{n}}}f_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{x}_{\boldsymbol{n},Q})\1_Q(\boldsymbol{x}).
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:cellwise} gives
\[
 \lVert f_{\boldsymbol{n}}-\widetilde g_{\boldsymbol{n}}\rVert_\infty
 \le\vartheta_0\lVert f\rVert_\infty.
\]
The function $\widetilde g_{\boldsymbol{n}}$ is constant on the cells of ${\mathcal D}_{\boldsymbol{n}}$, and therefore also on the cells of $\mathcal{Q}_{\beta(\boldsymbol{n})}$. By \eqref{8-1}, there exists a unique  $g_{\boldsymbol{n}}\in H_{\beta(\boldsymbol{n})}$ such that $\widetilde g_{\boldsymbol{n}}=g_{\boldsymbol{n}}\circ \pi$.


  Now  define
\[
  F:=\sum_{\boldsymbol{n}\in\mathcal{A}(f)}g_{\boldsymbol{n}}.
\]
Then
\[ F\in \sum_{\boldsymbol{n}\in\mathcal{A}(f)}  H_{\beta(\boldsymbol{n})}\subset V.\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:dlvp}(i) and $|\mathcal{A}(f)|\le(L+1)^d$,
\begin{align*}
 \lVert f-F\circ\pi\rVert_\infty
 &\le\sum_{\boldsymbol{n}\in\mathcal{A}(f)}\lVert f_{\boldsymbol{n}}-\widetilde g_{\boldsymbol{n}}\rVert_\infty\le(L+1)^d\vartheta_0\lVert f\rVert_\infty.
\end{align*}

label: lem:amplify
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put
\[
 m_0:=m_*(N,d,B,\eta_0),
 \qquad
 k:=\left\lceil\frac{\log(1/\eta)}{\log(1/\eta_0)}\right\rceil.
\]
Let $\xi^1, \xi^2, \ldots$ be iid random points drawn uniformly from $\mathbb T^d$.
Divide the first $km_0$ sample points into the independent blocks
\[
 X^{(j)}:=\{\xi^{(j-1)m_0+1},\ldots,\xi^{jm_0}\},
 \qquad 1\le j\le k.
\]
For each $j$, let $E_j$ be the event that $X^{(j)}$ is not a $B$-norming set for $\mathcal T(N,d)$. Then $\mathbf{P}(E_j)\le\eta_0$, and the events $E_1,\ldots,E_k$ are independent. Hence
\[
 \mathbf{P}(E_1\cap\cdots\cap E_k)\le\eta_0^k\le\eta.
\]
Let $X=\bigcup_{j=1}^k X^{(j)}$. If at least one of the blocks $X^{(j)}$ is a $B$-norming set, then their union  $X$ is also a $B$-norming set.  It follows that
 \begin{align*}{\mathbf P}& \Bigl\{  \|f\|_\infty\leq B\|f\|_{X}, \   \ \forall f\in\mathcal T(N,d)\Bigr\}\\
 &\ge {\mathbf P} \Bigl( \bigcup_{j=1}^k E_j^c\Bigr)={\mathbf P} \Bigl[\big(\bigcap_{j=1}^k E_j\big)^c\Bigr]=1-\mathbf{P}(E_1\cap\cdots\cap E_k)\\
  &\ge 1-\eta_0^k\ge 1-\eta.
 \end{align*}
 This means that  $X$ is a $B$-norming set for $\mathcal T(N, d)$ with probability at least $1-\eta$, and hence proves \eqref{8-5}.
